purpose: Upadacitinib is used to treat certain conditions where your immune system is overactive and causing inflammation. These include rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, atopic dermatitis (eczema), ulcerative colitis, and Crohn's disease. It helps reduce pain, swelling, and other symptoms so you can feel better and do more everyday activities.
how_it_works: Your immune system uses special proteins called JAK enzymes to send signals that cause inflammation. Upadacitinib blocks these JAK enzymes, which helps turn down the overactive immune response. Think of it like turning down the volume on the signals that are telling your body to stay inflamed.
common_side_effects: Upper respiratory infections like the common cold or sinus infections, acne, nausea, headache, fever, and increased cholesterol levels. Some people may also notice a higher risk of getting infections in general.
warnings: This medication carries serious warnings. It can increase your risk of serious infections, including tuberculosis and shingles, so your doctor will test you before starting. There is also an increased risk of blood clots, heart attack, stroke, and certain cancers including lymphoma. Do not take if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as some can interact with this drug. Regular blood tests and monitoring are important while on this medication.
typical_dosing: The dose depends on what condition is being treated and usually ranges from 15 mg to 45 mg taken by mouth once daily as an extended-release tablet. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes. Do not crush or chew the tablet — swallow it whole. You can take it with or without food.
